facts.fact: PRODUIR reports that on 30 April 2025 the decentralisation and land-planning ministry (MDAT) handed internet boxes and an internet subscription, with computers, printers and scanners, to all 38 communes of the Antananarivo agglomeration, the 3 DLAT and the SRAT Analamanga under MATAC/Hanorina phase 2.
facts.system: Internet subscription and internet boxes for the 38 communes under MATAC/Hanorina phase 2

facts.fact: The internet boxes are given so that the communes and the ministry's deconcentrated services can use the ministry's online building-permit tool MATAC/Hanorina, and the mayor of Itaosy says that with it everything is now online; 17 communes were already engaged and 21 are new in phase 2.
facts.system: Internet subscription and internet boxes for the 38 communes under MATAC/Hanorina phase 2

facts.fact: An internet subscription was provided to all 38 communes of the Antananarivo agglomeration on PRODUIR's account of 30 April 2025; no national total of communes is given, and all 38 are in Greater Antananarivo.
facts.system: Internet subscription and internet boxes for the 38 communes under MATAC/Hanorina phase 2

facts.fact: The equipment and internet subscription were handed over by the Ministère de la Décentralisation et de l'Aménagement du Territoire through its project PRODUIR, on 30 April 2025.
facts.system: Internet subscription and internet boxes for the 38 communes under MATAC/Hanorina phase 2

facts.fact: The handover of 30 April 2025 was made through PRODUIR, which the document states is financed by the World Bank; no domestic budget line is named.
facts.system: Internet subscription and internet boxes for the 38 communes under MATAC/Hanorina phase 2
